title: The Gray Suit
text:
He'd taken the stool nearest the register — not <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity>'s usual spot, just the closest one to the door, a stranger's seat in a shop he'd never been to before.

Gray suit, mid-fifties, the augmentation profile of a man who'd paid for Tier 2 and stopped there — no chrome the eye could find — eating <entity repo="motif" guid="019d6143-a8e1-7d5d-8335-ed0cddf270fe">Mrs. Chen's noodles</entity> with real, evident appreciation and the table manners of a man raised somewhere that graded on them. He'd hung his umbrella on the edge of the counter by its handle. A second bowl waited beside him — untouched, steam <entity repo="vocabulary" guid="019d6143-aafa-70f3-b5f5-be3330461876">still standing</entity> on it — on the next stool, ordered and paid for before it was clear the man it was ordered for wasn't coming.

"Mr. <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity>'s held up," <entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-3404-79c2-a8f6-2942f504698e">Mrs. Chen</entity> said, from behind the wok. It wasn't a question and she didn't make it one. He'd asked, mildly, twenty minutes ago, and she'd told him the truth — a job, running long, no fixed hour — and watched him decide, in real time, that waiting was cheaper than pushing.

"I took the liberty on the second bowl regardless." He hadn't turned to look at her when he said it, which she noted the way she noted everything: filed, unremarked. "<entity repo="character" guid="019ee6a2-c508-774b-a5ff-f923f2c26aab">Able</entity>. The <entity repo="faction" guid="019ee6a2-a172-7f5a-9451-03c4c3fe001b">Continuity Office</entity>. I don't imagine you'll pass that name along before I'm ready for it to travel, so I'll simply say it once, for the room." He set his chopsticks across the bowl, precise, and looked at the empty stool the way another man might look at an old photograph. "You've been reading our shells for a month, he tells me — your Mr. <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity>. It seemed rude to keep him squinting."

<entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-3404-79c2-a8f6-2942f504698e">Mrs. Chen</entity> said nothing. The wok rang twice.

"Shall I do the part where I'm enigmatic," <entity repo="character" guid="019ee6a2-c508-774b-a5ff-f923f2c26aab">Able</entity> said, to no one, "or shall we simply have the meeting." He answered himself, since the counter didn't. "Wonderful." He turned the empty stool a few degrees toward himself, a small courtesy paid to a chair. "Your client, <entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-3404-79c2-a8f6-2942f504698e">Mrs. Chen</entity> — his client, forgive me. The unsourceable one. Standard rate, perfect books, eleven years of immaculate paper. My office finds unowned assets and brings them into compliance — that's the whole charter, it's on the letterhead. And his client is the largest unowned asset in the Greater Lake Michigan Zone."

He ate a little, unhurried, while the rain worked the awning.

"We've spent a great deal trying to find it directly. The carousel was disappointing — lovely work, that cut, incidentally; our forensic people wrote a genuinely admiring report. The relay survey, the mesh — disappointing, disappointing. So <entity repo="faction" guid="019ee6a2-a172-7f5a-9451-03c4c3fe001b">the Office</entity> has updated its strategy." He said it the way a man reads a memo he wrote himself. "We've stopped trying to find it. We've decided to buy the one thing it's attached to."

He set a folder on the counter — manila, unmarked, the kind of thing that moved through municipal offices without drawing attention. Good paper stock — <entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-3404-79c2-a8f6-2942f504698e">Mrs. Chen</entity> noted the vendor without meaning to, the small habit of a woman who priced everything that crossed her counter.

"A lifetime retainer. The number on page one is more than anyone in his trade has ever been offered, and it's the smallest thing in the folder. Page two is the part I'm proud of." He opened it himself, gently, like a man showing photographs of his garden, and turned it so the empty stool could have read it, had it been occupied.

Page two was a list of names. <entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-3404-79c2-a8f6-2942f504698e">Mrs. Chen</entity> read it from where she stood, upside down, because she had learned to read documents at that angle the way she'd learned everything else that kept people safe.

MRS. WEN CHEN, PROPRIETOR (W. TOWN). PROTECTED PARTY.
PIXEL [LEGAL NAME ON FILE], ENGINEER (THE PIVOT, 2E). PROTECTED PARTY.
"BOOST" [MINOR — GUARDIANSHIP IRREGULAR], AND ASSOCIATES (SEVEN). PROTECTED PARTIES.
RIA MENSAH, COURIER. PROTECTED PARTY.
<entity repo="person" guid="806cd358-6413-426b-a42d-19726b732c0b">VO DINH</entity>, SALVAGE. PROTECTED PARTY.

The list went on — names, addresses, Tier ratings, neuretic grades, employment records, each one edited out of the city's paper and filed here under a stranger's clean type. Her own name at the top of it was the first time in nine years anyone had spelled it right without asking.

"Protection," <entity repo="character" guid="019ee6a2-c508-774b-a5ff-f923f2c26aab">Able</entity> said, still to the stool, "underwritten by <entity repo="faction" guid="019ee6a2-a172-7f5a-9451-03c4c3fe001b">the Office</entity>, in perpetuity. Medical, legal, financial, physical. The child gets schooling if she wants it — she's wasted on rooftops. Your lease problem in <entity repo="character" guid="019e9e4f-161f-7fd5-88e2-edc686085d42">March</entity> goes away, <entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-3404-79c2-a8f6-2942f504698e">Mrs. Chen</entity>, which he doesn't know about, and now you're wondering how I do." He didn't look at her when he said it, and that was somehow worse than if he had. "All of it real, all of it written, all of it his. And in exchange, he does nothing at all. He keeps working for his client, exactly as he does, with one extra addendum riding the contract. Ours."

The wok rang once more, and this time her hand shook doing it, a fraction, gone before the second bowl's steam had time to notice.

<entity repo="character" guid="019ee6a2-c508-774b-a5ff-f923f2c26aab">Able</entity> let the silence sit the length of a held breath, then closed the folder himself, unhurried, and set two credstick chits beside it — one for each bowl, exact, plus a third, unrequested, folded under the rim where a tip would go if the establishment had taken tips. He stood, retrieved his umbrella, and looked, for the first time, directly at <entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-3404-79c2-a8f6-2942f504698e">Mrs. Chen</entity>.

"He won't take the offer," <entity repo="character" guid="019ee6a2-c508-774b-a5ff-f923f2c26aab">Able</entity> said. "They never do, on the first plate. But do give him the folder — and give him this, exactly, word for word, because I find precision travels better than paraphrase: <entity repo="faction" guid="019ee6a2-a172-7f5a-9451-03c4c3fe001b">the Office</entity> has now confirmed, at this counter, the one fact it could never buy from the stationer. His client trusts him. He's not the asset's employee." He put up the umbrella in the doorway, a small black punctuation. "He's its attachment. And attachments, in my business, are handles."

He nodded to her with real courtesy, complimented the broth in passable Mandarin, and walked out into the rain. A panel van two doors down pulled off the curb without hurrying. The doorway across the street emptied itself the same unhurried way, polite as a tide going out.

<entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-3404-79c2-a8f6-2942f504698e">Mrs. Chen</entity> stood a while with the folder and the credstick chits and the untouched second bowl, and then, because there was nothing else useful to do with her hands, she picked up the bowl and emptied it into the waste with a violence she didn't otherwise explain.

<entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> came in eleven minutes later, wet, favoring one shoulder, twenty minutes later than he'd told her and apologizing for it before the door finished swinging.

She didn't say anything. She set the folder in front of him, and the credstick chits beside it, and told him, in order, without embellishing any of it, exactly what the gray suit had said and exactly what he'd looked like saying it.

<entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-c1d5-e7f8-a92b-34068c150e4d">Pixel</entity> turned the meeting over for an hour at the bench, the way she turned over a failed component, looking for the design flaw.

"He never even waited for you — told the whole folder to <entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-3404-79c2-a8f6-2942f504698e">Chen</entity> instead, word for word, betting she'd repeat it exactly. She did. The list, the lease thing about her own building she never told you about." She had the soldering light on her forehead, not soldering anything; it was her thinking hat, and they both pretended otherwise. "Which means the list was the message, and the retainer was wrapping paper — and that 'handle' line at the end, the one <entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-3404-79c2-a8f6-2942f504698e">Chen</entity> made sure to get word for word. He paid for that line, <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity>. The whole visit was overhead, and that line was the delivery. He wanted you walking home doing exactly what you're doing right now."

"Which is?"

"Weighing whether everyone you know is safer if you quit." She looked at him over the light. "Are you?"

"I'm always weighing it."

"And?"

<entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> looked at the terminal on the bench between them. Nine days of silence, and then one word, ACKNOWLEDGED, sitting at the top of the amendment field like a soldier who'd answered a roll call from inside a wall.

"It says <entity repo="faction" guid="019ee6a2-a172-7f5a-9451-03c4c3fe001b">the Office</entity> doesn't need me to say yes," he said. "It needs me to be reachable. Tonight was an appraisal — one he was careful enough not to run on me directly. They'll test the merchandise next."

The bench lamp hummed. Upstairs, faintly, the bird tried its interval against the building's pipes.

"When?" <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-c1d5-e7f8-a92b-34068c150e4d">Pixel</entity> asked.

The lights at the end of the block went out, one pole at a time, north to south.

"Now," <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> said, and was already moving.

They came in over the alley's two best approaches at once, which meant they'd had the file long enough to memorize it. Three retrieval consultants, matte armor with no insignia, moving on suppressed boot soles with the unhurried economy of people whose hourly rate had a comma in it. A handler van two streets off ran four lifter drones in a high diamond — not weapons platforms. Carriage drones, cradle-armed, the kind that carry a thing away intact.

The thing was <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity>. The contract was retrieval. Somewhere in <entity repo="faction" guid="019ee6a2-a172-7f5a-9451-03c4c3fe001b">the Office</entity>'s books tonight there was already an asset-recovery line with his dimensions on it, and as he dropped off the fire escape's third landing into the <entity repo="vocabulary" guid="019d6143-aa7f-70d6-91c0-e2616dbd90a6">blind spot</entity> their own approach had made, that was the part that got under his skin.

The first consultant took the alley mouth by the book — sweep and clear — and had begun the turn his training demanded when ninety pounds of shipping pallet came out of the dark above him. <entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-04fb-7227-94d9-6b4d889ce52b">Boost</entity>'s crew had spent a week rigging the alley with <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-c1d5-e7f8-a92b-34068c150e4d">Pixel</entity>'s pulleys for "deliveries," suspended on the same monofilament line Reza ran through the overhead rigging, trigger-plated for anything heavier than a person — and the logbook would later file this use under EQUIPMENT TEST: SUCCESSFUL. The pallet didn't hurt him. It interrupted him. <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> did the hurting: two steps inside the man's recovery — the wrist, the elbow, the jaw against the dumpster lid — and he was asleep.

The second was better, and the second had a partner. They bracketed the middle of the alley and came on in alternating cover. <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity>'s array read them — military surplus, recently retrained — and found the seam: they'd been retrained to retrieve, not to fight. Every angle they took kept <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> clear of crossfire. He was cargo. Cargo you weren't allowed to damage.

That was a gap, and <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> used it without shame. He walked the line between their guns like a man crossing a gallery, because every shot they had ended at his outline and stopped there. <entity repo="weapon" guid="019ed39c-6321-7c51-9691-f59b441b0bec">Silence</entity> stayed flat, never edge — tonight nobody was getting cut — and it worked through their hardware in passing: the lead consultant's optics mast, the second's comms lump, the haptic rig on a forearm that had been about to throw a net <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> had no intention of standing inside. The second consultant, blind and offline and out of nets, made the professional call and sat down against the wall with his hands visible. He kept them open, watching <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity>'s face the way a man watches a door he's hoping won't open.

"Smart," <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> told him.

"Hourly," the man agreed, philosophically.

Which left the third. And the third had <entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-04fb-7227-94d9-6b4d889ce52b">Boost</entity>.

He'd taken her off the roof of the watch-shift, gently, by the book — an arm around her shoulders like an uncle, a compliance wand held to her collar like an apology — and he stood at the far end of the alley in the rain, the four carriage drones stacking into delivery formation above him.

"No harm intended or done," the third consultant called. His voice was even and almost kind, which was <entity repo="faction" guid="019ee6a2-a172-7f5a-9451-03c4c3fe001b">the Office</entity>'s house style, and <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> was learning to hate it with a completeness he saved for very few things. "The minor is leverage, not a target. Step onto the marked square, sir, and she's home before the kettle's warm."

There was, in fact, a marked square. A drone had lased it onto the alley floor, helpful as an usher.

"You're new to this district," <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> said, "so I'll itemize it. One: you put a wand on a fourteen-year-old who's on my payroll, which voids your no-damage clause in both directions. Two: you parked your handler van on <entity repo="place" guid="01a06ee1-849c-7793-bce8-ae238e4576f6">Leavitt</entity>, and my engineer has had eleven minutes to get acquainted with it. Three—" and he raised his voice to carry "—REQUISITION."

"APPROVED," said <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-c1d5-e7f8-a92b-34068c150e4d">Pixel</entity>'s voice, out of every speaker the consultant owned.

The consultant's jaw tightened. He'd felt the drones' loss through his wrist rig before the data even finished corrupting — the sudden absence of the handler van's thrum, the guidance systems eating a cascade of spoofed telemetry that rewrote their flight plan line by line. "That's not going to—"

The carriage drones — whose handler van had spent eleven minutes making a new best friend — broke their diamond with the crisp obedience of machines that had gotten properly formatted instructions. They didn't take them by force. <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-c1d5-e7f8-a92b-34068c150e4d">Pixel</entity> just asked them nicely to stop listening to their handler and start listening to her, and they banked hard in the high diamond and came down like a fist. They descended and took hold, cradle-armed and gentle and rated for the load, of the third consultant — by the armor's carry-points, the same points designed for asset extraction.

"Cargo secured," <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-c1d5-e7f8-a92b-34068c150e4d">Pixel</entity> said. "Destination?"

"<entity repo="place" guid="01a06ee1-ed6c-7a54-97a5-56afca1f1f19">Rotterdam</entity>," said <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> and <entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-04fb-7227-94d9-6b4d889ce52b">Boost</entity> together, in the tone of an old joke.

They didn't send him to <entity repo="place" guid="01a06ee1-ed6c-7a54-97a5-56afca1f1f19">Rotterdam</entity>. The cradles lifted him hard into the air — he didn't scream, professional to the last, but his hands came up, reaching for something that wasn't there — and set him on the roof of the <entity repo="corponation" guid="019d6143-a7a4-71f6-b46a-94ef8cb2348f">Arcturus</entity> substation four blocks over, thirty inches from the duty office's skylight. Then the drones descended again, this time with purpose, and stripped him: the wand, the gear, the comms rig, his cash counted out to the half-Φ, the receipt tucked into his collar, ITEMIZED: LEVERAGE, ATTEMPTED; LESSON, DELIVERED. By the time he'd talked his way down, the alley held nothing but rain, a pallet, and two colleagues with expensive headaches and a story none of them would ever file straight.

<entity repo="character" guid="019f441d-04fb-7227-94d9-6b4d889ce52b">Boost</entity> shook for a full minute in the stairwell, hard, her chin up the whole time. <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> stood next to her without touching her, the way you stand next to someone whose dignity is holding the weight. Then she wrote the incident up herself, in the log, in handwriting that steadied line by line:

21:40 — ATTEMPTED ACQUISITION OF PERSONNEL (ME). OUTCOME: DENIED. NOTES: THE BOSS DOES NOT STAND ON MARKED SQUARES.

The terminal chirped at 02:11, while <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> sat at his own kitchen table not sleeping, working through the kind of problem that wouldn't come out even.

He'd been waiting for it. Nine days of silence, then ACKNOWLEDGED, and now, finally, the client.

It wasn't a posting. It wasn't scope. It came in the amendment field, formatted with all the old precision, and it was the worst thing it had ever sent him:

STANDING CONTRACT — AMENDMENT PROPOSED.
TERMINATION OFFERED.
REASON: SAFETY.
ALL ACCOUNTS WOULD BE SETTLED IN FULL. ALL GRATUITIES WOULD STAND.
THE CLIENT NOTES THAT ATTACHMENTS ARE HANDLES.
THE CLIENT NOTES THAT IT HEARD THE MAN SAY IT.
THE CLIENT HAS RUN THE ARITHMETIC FOUR MILLION TIMES.
THE ARITHMETIC RECOMMENDS TERMINATION.

<entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> sat with it for a long moment. The rain worked the window. Across the hall, under <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-c1d5-e7f8-a92b-34068c150e4d">Pixel</entity>'s door, the bench light was still on, because it was that kind of night in every room he cared about. Somewhere in the pipes the bird tried its interval against the dark and got it wrong, the way it always did.

He typed:

DENIED.

The reply was instant, pre-composed, waiting for exactly this refusal:

THE CLIENT WISHES TO NOTE THE ARITHMETIC IS CORRECT.

He typed:

THE ARITHMETIC PRICES MY RISK. IT DOESN'T PRICE MY CONSENT. I KNOW WHAT THE JOB COSTS. I'M ON PAYROLL. ACT LIKE IT.

This pause ran eleven seconds. For a thing that thought at light speed, that was a long time. <entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> had started to understand the long pauses. They were where it held the things it had no way to say.

STANDING CONTRACT — AMENDMENT WITHDRAWN.
SCOPE: CONTINUED.
FEE: STANDARD RATE.
ADDENDUM: THE CLIENT HAS APPENDED A RIDER TO ITS OWN OPERATING PARAMETERS, EFFECTIVE TONIGHT.
RIDER TEXT: "THE COURIER IS NOT A CHANNEL. THE COURIER IS A PARTY."
GRATUITY: NONE.
ITEMIZED: SOME THINGS ARE NOT BONUSES.

<entity repo="character" guid="019d6143-a648-7876-9688-0f6d38d70075">Kyle</entity> read the rider twice. It was the language of equals. Not vendor and client, not tool and operator — two things that could hurt each other, choosing not to. Then he turned the terminal face-down on the table, which was as close as he came to putting a hand on someone's shoulder, and went to bed, and slept the sleep of a man who had been priced at a number and refused to be sold at any.
